Investigation log
Scotland Yard case file · October 1926

Death at Blackwood Manor

11:05 p.m. Thomas Reed, the butler, finds Lord Edmund Blackwood dead at his desk. The storm has flooded the lane and taken down the telephone line. Until dawn, everyone who could have killed him is still inside the house.

Your task is to examine the rooms, build a defensible theory from physical evidence, and decide whether Blackwood died naturally or was murdered. Do not treat every suspicious fact as proof: several people in this house have something to hide.

Lady MargaretThe widow
Dr. Julian HaleFamily doctor
Clara FinchSecretary
Thomas ReedButler
Victor BlackwoodNephew

Investigation rule: the photographs are evidence scenes, not answer keys. Mark only what you believe you have actually located, and use the full case mode when you want interviews, testimony, timeline reconstruction, and a formal accusation.

Build your theory

A strong case must explain who, how, and why without ignoring contradictory evidence. This board saves your current hypothesis but does not tell you whether it is right.

Lady MargaretPotential inheritance and a private relationship. Test motive against opportunity and physical evidence.
Dr. HaleKnows digitalis and foxglove. Distinguish expertise from access to the actual poison source.
Clara FinchNear the study and aware of household movements. Separate what she saw from what she could have done.
Thomas ReedHandled the brandy and has a secret in the cellar books. Compare the decanter with the victim's glass.
Victor BlackwoodMoney trouble and a disputed alibi. Compare his story with the billiard room, boot room, and greenhouse.
